clue.text: General lookout a half-hearted TV viewer would keep?

definitions.meaning: a general brief to keep an eye on proceedings, as a lawyer does for an interested party

definitions.text: a half-hearted TV viewer would keep
definitions.meaning: someone only half interested in the screen watches briefly, i.e. keeps a brief spell of viewing

explanation.surface: Someone keeping half an eye on the television is mock-solemnly said to be on general lookout.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: a half-hearted viewer is only watching briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, the phrase names a mandate to monitor a case on someone's behalf: a general lookout.

clue.text: Densely populated area — a battleground for a colonial administrator

parts.note: a crowded maze of dwellings, like a network of rabbit burrows
the East Sussex town where the Battle of 1066 was fought

explanation.surface: A crowded district that was once a battlefield gets attached to a colonial official.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1066 battle took place near the town of that name in East Sussex, on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the first Governor-General of Bengal, the leading British colonial administrator in India.

clue.text: Aperture at end of boat for pin?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from boat

parts.note: an aperture is an opening or gap

explanation.surface: A query about the gap at the back of a boat that something slots into.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a peg in a boat's gunwale serving as a fulcrum for an oar, i.e. a pin.

clue.text: Eg screen idol's brother at opening of Hollywood complex

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, taken from Hollywood
complex suggests something intricately tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A film star's brother turns up at the start of some Hollywood development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' looks like a noun (a building complex) but signals an anagram of BROTHER AT plus H.
explanation.definitionFit: A swooned-over film star is an example of a figure who makes fans' pulses race.

clue.text: Harmful universal scam set up by old American

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are written upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal
a con is a swindle or scam
US stands for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: A damaging all-purpose swindle arranged by an elderly American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns U plus CON into NOCU.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a rare word for injurious or noxious, the opposite of innocuous.

clue.text: Back-room boys leaving home in outskirts of Brussels

indicators.note: in places the next pieces inside the letters taken from Brussels
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: someone leaving is off, i.e. departing
being at home is being in

explanation.surface: Backroom staff set off from home on the edges of the Belgian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Back-room boys is an idiom for technical experts or scientists working behind the scenes.

clue.text: Knowledgeable about some quaint observances

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of their letters are taken, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: Someone well versed in a few quaint customs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keen on or expert in something, as in being into jazz, is being knowledgeable about it.

clue.text: Reportedly battled with Galahad for some time?

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are as heard said, not as written

parts.note: battled is fought, and Sir Galahad was a knight of the Round Table

explanation.surface: A tale that someone once fought alongside Galahad for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fought knight', said aloud, sounds like the two-week word.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of fourteen days is an example of some time.

clue.text: At sea later, we dream about a Lake Poet

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the next pieces
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is a common map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Drifting on the sea afterwards, we fantasise about one of the Lake Poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Lake Poet' tempts a solver toward Wordsworth or Coleridge, but only 'Poet' defines; 'a Lake' gives AL, held by the anagram of LATER WE DREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: He was an English writer of verse, best known for 'The Listeners'.

clue.text: A judge returning with port wine

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, often just Rio, is a Brazilian port

indicators.note: returning means going back, so these letters are read in reverse

explanation.surface: A judge comes back with port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port wine' looks like one item, but port is RIO and wine alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Spanish red from the region of the same name, so a type of wine.

clue.text: Fair held in estate, perhaps -— one with a buffet

indicators.note: held in means enclosed by, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, hence the perhaps
a fete is a fair or outdoor festivity
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fair is staged on a country estate, with someone laying out a spread of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate' suggests land, but it is the estate car, a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service restaurant or counter is one sense of buffet.

clue.text: Notice clerk endlessly shifting class of mail

indicators.note: shifting means moving around, so these letters are rearranged
endlessly means the final letter of clerk is cut off

explanation.surface: A postal clerk is warned of changes to a category of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb or noun to be replaced, but it is anagram fodder with CLER.
explanation.definitionFit: E-mail is the computerised kind of mail, so the adjective names a class of it.

clue.text: Containers are rejected, provoking fit of pique in American

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: tins are metal containers

explanation.surface: Someone is in a huff because their containers have been turned away.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage a sulky state of irritation is a huff, a tantrum of pique.

clue.text: Person picking up girl, say, given very short measure?

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so the phrase is matched by sound

parts.note: one who meets Millie, a girl's name, is a Millie-meeter

explanation.surface: A man chatting up a girl is given a measly ration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking up' is collecting or meeting, giving a 'Millie meeter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousandth of a metre is a tiny unit of length, so a very short measure.

clue.text: Intuitive feelings revolutionary in early invaders

indicators.note: in places the revolutionary inside the invaders' name

parts.note: the Huns invaded Europe in the 4th and 5th centuries
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: Gut feelings that a revolutionary lurks among the ancient invaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Guesses based on instinct rather than evidence are intuitive feelings.

clue.text: Frightful thing left in youngster's disco!

indicators.note: frightful suggests a dreadful mess, so the letters of thing are jumbled
in places the left abbreviation inside the youngster

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or a junior scout, a youngster

explanation.surface: A dreadful thing was abandoned at a child's dance party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightful thing' reads as one phrase meaning a horror, but the adjective is the anagram signal working on the noun beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-opening venue for dancing to recorded music is a synonym for a disco.

clue.text: Groovy type, one performing with wife on board?

indicators.note: on board means taken aboard, so wife sits inside the performer

parts.note: a singer is one who performs

explanation.surface: A trendy entertainer performing with his wife aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship but means held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hip, fashionable, lively person of the sixties was a groovy type.

clue.text: Old soldiers with warning for a gentleman of Verona

parts.note: a sign can be a warning or omen
RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Veterans with a warning for an Italian gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old soldiers' reads as one unit, but splits into O and RE (the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps).
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Italian title for a man, the equivalent of sir or mister in Verona.

clue.text: Act of avoiding false perception, some say

indicators.note: some say means as pronounced by some speakers

parts.note: an illusion is a false perception

explanation.surface: Some claim that dodging is just a trick of the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasion or escaping by cleverness is an act of avoiding.

clue.text: Painter's requisite a citizen of Riga kept in gym?

indicators.note: kept in means enclosed, so the letters go inside the gym abbreviation

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym
a Lett is a Latvian, and Riga is Latvia's capital

explanation.surface: A Latvian keeps the artist's essential kit in the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: The board on which an artist mixes colours is a painter's essential tool.

clue.text: Sufferer showing forbearance

definitions.meaning: a person under medical care, someone suffering an illness
tolerant and calm in the face of delay or trouble

explanation.surface: A sick person remaining calm and enduring.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for someone receiving treatment and an adjective for enduring calmly.

clue.text: Returned nine letters? This is the ninth abroad

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: A to I covers the first nine letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone sends back nine letters and notes one is the ninth in a foreign script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nine letters' are not nine of anything sent in the post: A to I spans nine letters, giving ATOI.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, so the ninth letter abroad.

clue.text: Graduate touring university developed limited sources of info

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the graduate wraps the following letters

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A graduate on a university tour builds up a narrow set of information sources.
explanation.definitionFit: Combined media such as text, video and sound are sources of information.

clue.text: Bigmouth: associate of 20

definitions.meaning: a river's broad fan-shaped mouth where it meets the sea
20 across is a Greek letter; this is a fellow Greek letter, the fourth

explanation.surface: A loudmouth who keeps company with the person at number 20.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the landform at a river's outlet and the fourth Greek letter, a companion of iota.

clue.text: Cautious taking route across river

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the route goes round the river letter

parts.note: a way is a route

explanation.surface: Someone careful about taking a path across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on guard against danger is a synonym of cautious.

clue.text: Vehicle lass is astride, easy at first to kick-start

indicators.note: astride means straddling, so the lass and is sit either side of the vehicle

parts.note: a gal is a girl or lass
a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of easy is used

explanation.surface: A girl sits astride a vehicle that's easy enough to kick-start, like a motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock into action or stimulate is to jolt something into motion, i.e. kick-start it.

clue.text: A slovenly woman making a comeback in Oklahoma?

indicators.note: a comeback means returning, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: an old sense of slut is a slovenly, untidy woman

explanation.surface: An untidy woman returns to the scene somewhere in Oklahoma.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a city in the US state of Oklahoma, so a place found in Oklahoma, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Intolerable: too much for those of sallow complexion

definitions.text: too much for those of sallow complexion
definitions.meaning: read literally: past the colour of the pale-faced

explanation.surface: Something unbearable, too much even for the sickly-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pale was the area around Dublin under English rule; outside it lay the unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means outside the bounds of acceptable conduct, so unacceptable or unbearable.
